---
title: Getting a security review without authority
tags: influence, collaboration, cross-team
---

Situation: A new authentication flow needed a security review before launch. The security team
had a six-week backlog and we had a two-week deadline, and they did not report to anyone on my
side.

Task: Get a real review in time without trying to jump their queue by escalation.

Action: I did the work that made their job small: wrote the threat model in their template,
listed the specific decisions I wanted validated, pre-answered their standard checklist, and
asked for a thirty-minute session instead of a full review.

Result: They agreed, the session found one real issue, a token lifetime set too long, which we
fixed the same day, and we launched on time. My rule since: make the other team's yes as cheap as
possible.
